llm.summary: The skill’s files and instructions largely match a UI design assistant, but a static scan flagged a possible system-prompt override in SKILL.md (prompt‑injection risk) and the runtime instructions/scripts could be used to influence agent behavior — review before installing.

dimensions.detail: Name/description, the bundled CSV knowledge base, and the scripts (search.py, core.py, design_system.py) are coherent for a local UI design helper that generates design systems and maps them to code. No unrelated credentials, binaries, or external services are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to run the included Python scripts against the local data, which is expected. However the pre-scan found a 'system-prompt-override' pattern in SKILL.md (prompt-injection). The SKILL.md contains a YAML header and large prose instructions that could be used to steer agent/system behavior if the platform treats SKILL.md content as higher-privilege instructions. The example CLI lines reference an explicit path ('python3 skills/ui-craft-pro/scripts/search.py') that may not match runtime sandbox paths — minor operational inconsistency but worth checking.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (no external downloads). That lowers supply-chain risk. But the skill bundle includes executable Python scripts and a large local data set; running those scripts will execute code that lives in the skill. The provided code snippet (data/_sync_all.py) shows only local CSV manipulation and no network calls, but the full scripts should be inspected for outgoing network or subprocess behavior before execution.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables, no credentials, and no config paths. The absence of secrets/credentials is appropriate for a local UI/design assistant.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and user-invocable:true (normal). The skill does not declare system-wide modifications or special persistence. Autonomous invocation is allowed by default on the platform; that is expected but increases impact if the skill contains manipulative instructions — combine this with the prompt-injection signal when deciding.

dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package mostly looks like a coherent offline UI design skill (local CSVs + Python scripts), but a prompt-injection pattern was detected in SKILL.md. Before installing or granting execution rights: 1) Review SKILL.md end-to-end for any lines that attempt to change system prompts, escalate privileges, or instruct the agent to ignore platform rules. 2) Inspect scripts/search.py, scripts/core.py, and scripts/design_system.py for network calls, subprocess.exec/OS calls, or code that writes outside the skill folder. 3) If possible run the scripts in an isolated sandbox (no network) first to observe behavior. 4) Confirm the platform’s runtime path expectations (the CLI examples use a 'skills/ui-craft-pro/…' path that may be inaccurate). 5) If you lack the ability to audit the code, be cautious: do not allow the skill to run autonomously or in always-on mode, and avoid giving it access to sensitive data or credentials. If you want, I can scan the remaining truncated script files for network or subprocess calls and summarize any findings.
llm.findings: [system-prompt-override] unexpected: SKILL.md contains content that triggered a 'system-prompt-override' pattern scan. For a UI design helper, embedding directives aimed at altering the agent's system prompt or execution policy is not necessary and is unexpected. This could be benign (overly prescriptive guidance) or an attempt to manipulate agent behavior; review SKILL.md and confirm how the platform treats skill instruction headers.
